radiology_report:
Radboudumc
Department of Radiology
Date: 12 December 2024
Exam: Multiparametric MRI prostate
Clinical indication: PSA 7.6 ng/mL, previous biopsy Gleason 3+3. Evaluate for focal lesion.

FINDINGS:
Prostate volume: 63.0 mL. T2-weighted images demonstrate a focal hypo-intense lesion in the peripheral zone at the base/mid right, measuring approximately 12 mm in greatest dimension. On DWI, the lesion shows restricted diffusion with high signal on b=1400 and corresponding low ADC values. Dynamic contrast-enhanced sequences reveal early, intense enhancement of the same region.

IMPRESSION:
PI-RADS v2.1: 5 (highly suspicious for clinically significant prostate cancer).
PSA density: 0.121 ng/mL/mL.
Clinical T stage: cT2a.
csPCa predicted probability 0.0.

previous_notes.author: Dr. P. van Dijk (GP)
previous_notes.text: Patient presented with elevated PSA of 3.5 ng/mL. DRE was unremarkable. MRI showed PI-RADS 4 lesion. Systematic biopsy performed, revealing Gleason 3+3 ISUP GG1. Discussed active surveillance versus treatment. Patient opted for surveillance with 6-monthly PSA monitoring and repeat MRI in 12 months.

pathology_report:
Biopsy 1 (May 2024): Histological examination reveals adenocarcinoma of the prostate, Gleason score 3+3, ISUP grade group 1. The growth pattern is acinar. No cribriform or intraductal patterns identified. Perineural invasion is present. The tumour is located in the peripheral zone, base/mid right.

Biopsy 2 (December 2024): Histological examination reveals adenocarcinoma of the prostate, Gleason score 3+3, ISUP grade group 1. The growth pattern is acinar. No cribriform or intraductal patterns identified. Perineural invasion is present. The tumour is located in the peripheral zone, base/mid right.

Summary: The histological findings remain stable across both timepoints, showing persistent low-grade disease with perineural invasion.

AI-predicted ISUP grade group (digital pathology): grade group 2.
